thread.title: Volleyball: 'Cats look to continue upward trajectory in tricky conference
thread.title_full: Volleyball: 'Cats look to continue upward trajectory in tricky conference

author: Isaiah Steinberg, Senior Staffer
title: Volleyball: 'Cats look to continue upward trajectory in tricky conference
text:
Fresh off a resounding resurgence in 2025, the ’Cats enter this season with clear momentum.
After a dismal 2024 season that saw NU finish 5-23 overall, coach Tim Nollan’s squad bounced back last year, finishing 17-15 and rising three places on the Big Ten leaderboard with a 7-13 conference record.
Though that performance still placed them 14th — well within the bottom half of arguably the toughest conference in women’s volleyball — the ’Cats reliably bested teams ranked below them and rallied to upset Michigan without the help of then-senior outside hitter Rylen Reid.
Last season, NU demonstrated a balanced offense, excellent serving and a versatile rotation overall. Weaknesses included lackluster blocking, a clear talent gap against elite opponents and an inability to convert some close matches into wins.
Nollan made use of the transfer portal in his first two seasons, culminating in a team-leading 371 kills by outside hitter Ayah Elnady, a former Kansas Jayhawk. But much of the team’s success came from veterans like Reid and setters Sienna Noordermeer and Lauren Carter.
NU led the conference in aces largely thanks to Carter and Elnady, whose absences could hinder the ’Cats behind the service line this season.
With Reid and Noordermeer also departing — along with impact players like outside hitters Buse Hazan and Kathryn Randorf — the ’Cats will have to look to young talent this season, allowing Nollan to implement his preferred strategy of recruitment and retention over the portal.
Enter six incoming freshmen: middle blockers Hayley Schaaf and Maya Stillwell, outside hitters Simone Huarte and Clara Schramm, and setters Kaitlyn Bodnar and Ellie Stiernagle — NU’s largest incoming class since 2018.
Both of the ’Cats setters this season will be freshmen. Stiernagle, who is ranked No. 78 in the country on Prep Dig, will need to adjust quickly if NU is to make a run in the inaugural Big Ten Tournament in November.
With the addition of Stiernagle, No. 153-ranked Stillwell and No. 198-ranked Schaaf, the ’Cats scored their highest number of nationally ranked players since 2022.
On the transfer side, Utah State’s Mara Štiglic tallied a team-high 431 kills for the Aggies last season — more than any Wildcat. With Štiglic coming to Evanston as a junior, she could prove an offensive stalwart for several years.
From Tennessee, the ’Cats will also gain Cate Schnell, who joins an already strong roster of eight other outside hitters.
Replacing NU’s veteran production will be no easy task. Rising sophomore Bella Bullington and rising senior Campbell Paris — numbers three and four on kills in 2025 — will need to step up to the challenge.
If last season established a strong foundation for the ’Cats, this one will determine whether they can build on it.
